newsitem.title: UK: Shake-out seen for overcrowded UK DIY market.
newsitem.headline: Shake-out seen for overcrowded UK DIY market.

text.p: Britain's do-it-yourself retailers are enjoying an upturn this year from the housing market recovery, but overcapacity in the sector remains and store closures lie ahead, according to a new report published on Monday.

Retail consultants Verdict expected market leaders in DIY retailing would continue to capture the lion's share of the growth in the market, while weaker players would struggle because of overcapacity.
"A comprehensive rationalisation to solve this problem did not occur over the recessionary years," Verdict said.
Weaker retailers have some underperforming stores to which they are tied by long lease commitments. "Their losses have also been borne by large retail parent companies with deep pockets."
Verdict said while market leader B&Q, owned by Kingfisher Plc, had consolidated its position, Do It All, part of Boots Co Plc, remained one of the biggest losers in the sector.
"Do It All is failing to attract enough customers into its stores and/or to encourage them to spend enough - sales per square foot is roughly two-thirds that of B&Q," Verdict said.
